MERIDIAN MECHANICAL OF TEXAS, LLC

EMPLOYEE HANDBOOK ADDENDUM
STATE-SPECIFIC POLICIES AND PROCEDURES

Effective Date: January 1, 2025

This Addendum to the Employee Handbook of Meridian Mechanical of Texas, LLC (hereinafter "Company"), with principal offices located at 4721 Westpark Drive, Suite 240, Houston, Texas 77042, sets forth additional policies and procedures applicable to all employees working in the State of Texas. This Addendum supersedes any conflicting provisions in the general Employee Handbook and shall be effective as of January 1, 2025. All employees are required to acknowledge receipt and understanding of this Addendum.

1. FINAL PAY AND WAGE REQUIREMENTS

The Company is committed to compliance with the Texas Labor Code and all applicable federal wage and hour laws. All compensation earned by employees shall be paid in full on the regular established payroll schedule, which occurs every other Friday.

1.1 Payment Upon Separation. Upon termination of employment, whether voluntary or involuntary, the Company shall pay all earned and unpaid wages due to the employee no later than the next regular payday following the date of separation, or if no regular payday is established, no later than the thirtieth (30th) calendar day following the last day of employment, whichever occurs first. This requirement applies to all accrued but unused paid time off (PTO) to the extent required by Company policy and applicable law. Employees who terminate employment must submit all Company property, including tools, vehicles, uniforms, and identification cards, before final wages are distributed.

1.2 Wage Deductions. The Company may only deduct from an employee's wages those deductions expressly permitted by the Texas Labor Code and federal law. Permissible deductions include federal and state income tax withholding, Social Security and Medicare taxes, court-ordered garnishments, and authorized payroll deductions for benefits. Deductions for tools, equipment, uniforms, or damage to Company property are prohibited unless the employee has expressly authorized such deductions in writing and the deduction does not reduce the employee's wages below the applicable minimum wage for the time period in question.

1.3 Pay Stubs. The Company shall provide each employee with an itemized pay stub for each pay period showing gross wages, all deductions, net pay, and year-to-date totals. Pay stubs may be provided electronically through the Company's payroll system or in printed form upon request.

1.4 Final Paycheck Delivery. Final paychecks upon separation shall be delivered to the employee in person at the Company's Houston office, or by certified mail to the employee's last known address on file, at the Company's option. The Company shall notify the employee of the method and anticipated delivery date in writing.

2. JURY DUTY AND VOTING LEAVE

2.1 Jury Duty Leave. Employees summoned for jury duty are encouraged to fulfill this important civic obligation. Upon receipt of a jury summons, the employee must provide a copy to Human Resources within two (2) business days. The Company shall permit employees to take necessary time off for jury selection and jury service without penalty or loss of regular compensation for the first three (3) days of jury service in any twelve-month period. After three days, continued absence for jury duty shall be treated in accordance with the Company's leave policies and applicable state and federal law.

2.2 Juror Status and Termination. The Company shall not discharge, threaten, intimidate, or coerce any employee because the employee has been summoned for or has served on a jury. Employees returning from jury duty shall be restored to their regular position or a substantially similar position with equivalent pay, benefits, and terms of employment. Any employee who believes they have been subjected to adverse action due to jury service should report the matter to Human Resources immediately.

2.3 Voting Leave. Employees are entitled to reasonable time off to vote in any federal, state, or local election. Under Texas Election Code Section 276.004, employees may take up to two (2) hours of paid leave during early voting or election day to vote, provided the employee has not had sufficient opportunity to vote before or after working hours. Employees should notify their supervisor in advance when possible and shall be permitted to take this leave during their regular work schedule without loss of pay or benefits.

3. HEAT STRESS PREVENTION FOR FIELD CREWS

The Company recognizes that employees working in outdoor conditions or in hot environments, particularly those in the HVAC service and repair industry, face significant heat-related health risks. The Company is committed to implementing comprehensive heat stress prevention measures to protect the health and safety of all field personnel.

3.1 Heat Stress Safety Program. The Company maintains a Heat Stress Prevention Program applicable to all field crews, including HVAC technicians, apprentices, helpers, and service dispatchers who work in elevated temperature environments. This Program complies with all applicable OSHA regulations and industry standards.

3.2 Hydration and Rest. During work in hot conditions, the Company shall provide:

(a) Adequate quantities of clean, cool drinking water at all job sites. Employees are encouraged to drink water frequently throughout the day, even if not thirsty, at a minimum rate of approximately eight ounces (8 oz.) every fifteen (15) to twenty (20) minutes;

(b) Frequent rest breaks in shaded or air-conditioned areas. Employees working in temperatures exceeding 95°F shall be permitted a minimum of ten (10) minute rest breaks every hour, during which time employees should remain in a cool environment;

(c) Flexible scheduling options when weather conditions are extreme, including the possibility of modified start times, adjusted work hours, or work postponement.

3.3 Medical Monitoring and Acclimatization. New employees and those returning from extended absence shall be provided with a period of acclimatization lasting a minimum of seven (7) working days, during which work intensity and duration shall be gradually increased. Supervisors shall monitor employees for signs of heat-related illness, including excessive fatigue, dizziness, nausea, or confusion, and shall immediately move any employee displaying these symptoms to a cool location and contact emergency medical services if necessary.

3.4 Personal Protective Equipment. While the Company recognizes that certain protective equipment may increase heat stress, necessary equipment shall be worn as required for safety. The Company shall provide lightweight, breathable options when available and shall adjust work schedules and break frequencies to accommodate required protective equipment use.

3.5 Heat Illness Reporting. Any employee who experiences or witnesses a heat-related illness at a job site must immediately report the incident to their supervisor and to Human Resources. The Company shall not retaliate against any employee for reporting heat-related safety concerns or for declining work under conditions the employee reasonably believes pose a serious health risk.

4. FIREARMS AND WEAPONS IN VEHICLES

4.1 Legal Authority. In accordance with Texas Labor Code Section 52.061, the Company acknowledges that employees have the right to store firearms and other weapons in a locked motor vehicle on Company premises or at job sites, provided such vehicle is parked in a location where the employee has a right to park.

4.2 Company Property Restrictions. Notwithstanding the protections afforded by Section 52.061, firearms, weapons, and ammunition are strictly prohibited:

(a) Within Company-owned or Company-controlled vehicles;

(b) In Company offices, service centers, or administrative facilities;

(c) On the person of any employee while performing work duties;

(d) Within the Company's secure tool storage facilities.

4.3 Secure Storage in Personal Vehicles. Employees who choose to store a firearm or other weapon in their personal vehicle while at a Company job site or facility must:

(a) Keep the firearm or weapon secured in a locked vehicle or locked container;

(b) Ensure the firearm or weapon is not accessible to other employees, the public, or minors;

(c) Not bring the firearm or weapon into any Company building or work area;

(d) Ensure compliance with all applicable federal and Texas firearms laws.

4.4 Workplace Violence Prevention. The Company maintains a zero-tolerance policy regarding workplace violence, threats, or intimidation. Possession of a firearm or weapon does not extend to any conduct in violation of the Company's Workplace Violence Prevention policy or any conduct that threatens the safety of employees, customers, or the public. Any employee who displays, brandishes, or threatens to use a firearm or weapon in the workplace shall be subject to immediate disciplinary action up to and including termination.

4.5 Company-Provided Vehicles. Firearms, weapons, and ammunition shall never be transported in Company-provided vehicles, including vans, trucks, and service vehicles. Company vehicles may be subject to inspection by management personnel, and the discovery of firearms or weapons in Company vehicles shall result in immediate disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment.

5. RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS

5.1 Applicability of Texas Law. Any restrictive covenants, non-competition agreements, non-solicitation provisions, or confidentiality agreements entered into by employees are governed exclusively by the Texas Business and Commerce Code Sections 15.50 through 15.52. The Company's use of such agreements is limited to those provisions permitted under Texas law.

5.2 Enforceability Standards. All restrictive covenants must meet the enforceability standards set forth in Texas Business and Commerce Code Section 15.50, including the requirement that such covenants be ancillary to an otherwise enforceable agreement, such as an employment agreement or separation agreement, and must be reasonable in temporal scope, geographical area, and line of business.

5.3 Acknowledged Provisions. Employees should be aware that any restrictive covenant provisions contained in their employment agreement or other Company documents are subject to the standards and limitations imposed by Texas law. The Company shall not attempt to enforce any restrictive covenant that does not meet the requirements of Texas Business and Commerce Code Sections 15.50-15.52.

5.4 Legal Review. Employees who have signed restrictive covenant agreements and have questions regarding the enforceability or scope of such agreements are encouraged to consult with legal counsel. The Company does not represent that any particular restrictive covenant is enforceable under Texas law, and any employee believing a covenant is overly broad or unenforceable may challenge such enforcement in accordance with applicable legal procedures.
